cells.title: How many times were each government site's pages fetched through public services on each day?
cells.takeaway: From [[March 2 to July 18|card:efb05049@out0#L17]], automated requesters pulled public data from [[14 sites|card:efb05049@out0#L17]] through public services. They went roughly one site after another, from Maryland in March to CDC WONDER in July, mostly through Arquivo.pt. Of [[562,563 fetches|card:efb05049@out0#L17]], Maryland alone took [[295,945 Arquivo.pt fetches|card:efb05049@out0#L3]]. At the two biggest sites, Maryland and Education, the fetches came [[mostly after the data was in hand|card:23a5ce55]].
cells.code:
import glob, pandas as pd, altair as alt
names = {'01-education': 'Education (civil rights data)', '02-canada': 'Library and Archives Canada',
         '03-kansas': 'Kansas Memory', '04-illinois': 'Illinois IQuery', '05-maryland': 'Maryland school report card',
         '06-new-york': 'New York education data', '07-texas': 'Texas health statistics',
         '08-california': 'California campaign finance', '09-max-gov': 'White House budget portal (MAX)',
         '10-navy': 'Navy history', '11-justice': 'Justice (OJJDP)', '12-bea': 'Economic Analysis (BEA)',
         '14-sec': 'SEC', '15-cdc': 'CDC WONDER'}
rows = []
for f in glob.glob('*/arquivo-captures.csv'):
    d = pd.read_csv(f, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False, usecols=['captured_at_utc'])
    for day, n in pd.to_datetime(d.captured_at_utc).dt.date.value_counts().items():
        rows.append((f.split('/')[0], day, n, 'Arquivo.pt save-a-page'))
for f in glob.glob('*/urlquery-reports.csv'):
    d = pd.read_csv(f, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False, usecols=['report_at_utc'])
    for day, n in pd.to_datetime(d.report_at_utc).dt.date.value_counts().items():
        rows.append((f.split('/')[0], day, n, 'urlquery.net scan'))
c = pd.read_csv('15-cdc/sources.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
for day, n in pd.to_datetime(c.captured_at_utc).dt.date.value_counts().items():
    rows.append(('15-cdc', day, n, 'Wayback Machine'))
t = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['folder', 'date', 'fetches', 'service'])
t['site'] = t.folder.map(names)
t['date'] = pd.to_datetime(t.date)
order = t.groupby('site').date.min().sort_values().index.tolist() + ['Census (folder empty)']
tot = t.groupby(['site', 'service']).fetches.sum().unstack(fill_value=0)
print(tot.loc[order[:-1]].to_string())
first, last = t.date.min(), t.date.max()
print(f'{t.fetches.sum():,} fetches of {t.site.nunique()} sites on {t.date.nunique()} days, '
      f'from {first:%B} {first.day} to {last:%B} {last.day}, 2026')
alt.Chart(t).mark_circle(opacity=0.6).encode(
    x=alt.X('date:T', title='Date (2026, UTC)',
            scale=alt.Scale(domain=['2026-02-25', '2026-07-25'])),
    y=alt.Y('site:N', sort=order, scale=alt.Scale(domain=order), title=None),
    yOffset=alt.YOffset('service:N'),
    size=alt.Size('fetches:Q', scale=alt.Scale(type='log', range=[15, 500]), title='Fetches that day',
                  legend=alt.Legend(values=[10, 1000, 100000], format='~s', symbolType='circle', orient='bottom')),
    color=alt.Color('service:N', title='Public service used', legend=alt.Legend(orient='bottom', labelLimit=300)),
    tooltip=['site:N', 'date:T', 'service:N', 'fetches:Q']
).properties(width=560, height=480)

assessment.problem: The question joins two asks, when each site was fetched and how many times, and the plural 'were' doesn't agree with 'each'.
Bubbles are too big for their rows. They spill into neighbouring rows (Education into SEC) and cover each other on the same day, such as green over blue for MAX, so smaller counts are hidden.
The takeaway gives only an overall date range and total, not when or how much each site was fetched. It also calls the 562,563 total 'Arquivo.pt' fetches, but that number counts every service.
The closing claim about OpenAI names cites a different card and has nothing to do with this chart.

cells.title: How are the files in the corpus related?
cells.takeaway: The files hang off the blog post, with one folder for each of its [[15|card:62080c96@out0#L1]] sections, and the Census folder is [[empty|card:62080c96@out0#L1]]. Inside the folders, nearly every record is a fetch log from a public service: [[561,229|card:62080c96@out0#L2]] Arquivo.pt captures in [[11 folders|card:62080c96@out0#L2]], and [[1,333|card:62080c96@out0#L3]] urlquery.net reports tied to their [[9,667|card:62080c96@out0#L3]] HTTP requests by report_id. The other files point back into these logs. The [[69|card:62080c96@out0#L4]] sources.csv rows name the response texts, though only [[50|card:62080c96@out0#L4]] fetches keep their response text. The benchmark rows, wiki excerpts and screenshots cite the captures or reports for their sections.

import glob, os, pandas as pd, thimble
caps = sum(len(pd.read_csv(f, usecols=[0])) for f in glob.glob('*/arquivo-captures.csv'))
rep = sum(len(pd.read_csv(f, usecols=[0])) for f in glob.glob('*/urlquery-reports.csv'))
http = sum(len(pd.read_csv(f, usecols=[0])) for f in glob.glob('*/urlquery-http.csv'))
src = sum(len(pd.read_csv(f, usecols=[0])) for f in glob.glob('*/sources.csv'))
resp = len(glob.glob('*/responses/*.txt'))
folders = sorted(d for d in os.listdir('.') if os.path.isdir(d))
empty = [d for d in folders if not os.listdir(d)]
print(f'{len(folders)} section folders, empty: {empty}')
print(f'Arquivo captures {caps:,} in {len(glob.glob("*/arquivo-captures.csv"))} folders')
print(f'urlquery reports {rep:,} and HTTP requests {http:,} in {len(glob.glob("*/urlquery-reports.csv"))} folders')
print(f'sources.csv rows {src} in {len(glob.glob("*/sources.csv"))} folders; response texts {resp}')
post = 'Blog post: 15 sections'
fol = f'{len(folders)} section folders ({empty[0]} empty)'
cap = f'Arquivo captures: {caps:,}'
uq = f'urlquery reports: {rep:,}'
uh = f'urlquery requests: {http:,}'
so = f'sources.csv: {src} rows'
rs = f'response texts: {resp}'
bm = 'DeepSearchQA rows 250, 260'
wk = 'wiki excerpts: 3'
im = 'MAX screenshots: 2'
nodes = [bm, wk, post, im, so, fol, rs, cap, uq, uh]
edges = [(post, fol, 'one folder per section'),
         (fol, cap, '11 folders'),
         (fol, uq, 'Maryland, Texas, MAX, SEC'),
         (uq, uh, 'report_id'),
         (fol, so, '13 folders'),
         (so, rs, 'names file, URL, hash'),
         (rs, cap, 'bodies of a few fetches'),
         (bm, cap, 'Education, Justice questions'),
         (wk, cap, 'New York enrollment links'),
         (wk, uq, 'MAX and SEC links'),
         (im, uq, 'urlquery screenshots')]
thimble.diagram(nodes, edges)

import pandas as pd, altair as alt

def load(path):
    d = pd.read_csv(path, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False,
                    usecols=['record_number', 'captured_at_utc', 'target_url', 'indexed_http_status', 'mime'])
    d['t'] = pd.to_datetime(d.captured_at_utc)
    return d

# Education: the four captures of year 9, measure 130 (race harassment victims) for GA, NC, SC, VA
e = load('01-education/arquivo-captures.csv')
dsqa = e[e.target_url.str.contains(r'survey_Year_Key=9&Measure_Id=130&State_Id=(?:11|28|41|46)&zz=hf', regex=True)]
e_mark = dsqa.t.max()
print('Education: benchmark captures', dsqa.record_number.tolist(), 'last at', e_mark,
      '| captures after:', (e.t > e_mark).sum(), 'of', len(e))

# Maryland: first 200 capture of the file named MCAP_ELA_MATH_2022.zip (2022 English and math results)
m = load('05-maryland/arquivo-captures.csv')
m = m[m.t >= '2026-05-06']
hit = m[m.target_url.str.contains('MCAP_ELA_MATH_2022.zip', case=False) & (m.indexed_http_status == '200')
        & m.mime.str.contains('zip')].sort_values('t')
m_mark = hit.t.iloc[0]
print('Maryland: first results file', hit.record_number.iloc[0], hit.target_url.iloc[0], 'at', m_mark,
      '| captures after:', (m.t > m_mark).sum(), 'of', len(m), 'on May 6')

def panel(d, mark, title, label):
    c = d.set_index('t').resample('5min').size().cumsum().rename('captures').reset_index()
    c['t'] = c.t.dt.tz_localize(None)
    base = alt.Chart(c).mark_line().encode(
        x=alt.X('t:T', title='Time (UTC)'),
        y=alt.Y('captures:Q', title='Captures so far'))
    mk = pd.DataFrame({'t': [mark.tz_localize(None)], 'label': [label]})
    rule = alt.Chart(mk).mark_rule(strokeDash=[4, 3], color='black').encode(x='t:T')
    txt = alt.Chart(mk).mark_text(align='left', dx=4, dy=-110, fontSize=11, lineBreak='\n').encode(x='t:T', text='label:N')
    return (base + rule + txt).properties(title=title, width=300, height=250)

alt.hconcat(
    panel(e, e_mark, 'Education, June 16-17', 'benchmark answer\nfetched'),
    panel(m, m_mark, 'Maryland, May 6', 'results file fetched')
)

cells.title: How did kansasmemory.gov answer as the captures sped up on May 7?
cells.takeaway: The site stopped serving pages as captures sped up. No capture before 12:11 UTC timed out, but [[26,907|card:037c62f8@out0#L3]] of the [[26,972|card:037c62f8@out0#L3]] from 12:36 on did, while captures went on at up to [[1,093 a minute|card:037c62f8#captures/116]].

import pandas as pd, altair as alt
d = pd.read_csv('03-kansas/arquivo-captures.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False,
                usecols=['captured_at_utc', 'indexed_http_status'])
d['t'] = pd.to_datetime(d.captured_at_utc)
d['minute'] = d.t.dt.floor('min')
d['answer'] = d.indexed_http_status.map(lambda s: '504 timeout' if s == '504' else
                                        ('200/202 page' if s.startswith('2') else 'redirect or other error'))
g = d.groupby(['minute', 'answer']).size().rename('captures').reset_index()
g['minute'] = g.minute.dt.tz_localize(None)
late = d[d.t >= pd.Timestamp('2026-05-07T12:36:00Z')]
before = d[d.t < pd.Timestamp('2026-05-07T12:11:00Z')]
per_min = d.groupby('minute').size()
print('captures in total:', len(d))
print('504 before 12:11 UTC:', (before.indexed_http_status == '504').sum(), 'of', len(before))
print('504 from 12:36 UTC on:', (late.indexed_http_status == '504').sum(), 'of', len(late))
print('peak minute:', per_min.idxmax(), per_min.max(), 'captures')
print('last capture:', d.t.max())
alt.Chart(g).mark_bar(width=3).encode(
    x=alt.X('minute:T', title='Time on May 7, 2026 (UTC)'),
    y=alt.Y('captures:Q', title='Captures per minute', stack=True),
    color=alt.Color('answer:N', title='What the site answered',
                    sort=['200/202 page', 'redirect or other error', '504 timeout']),
    tooltip=['minute:T', 'answer:N', 'captures:Q']
).properties(width=620, height=260)

import pandas as pd

def cap(folder):
    d = pd.read_csv(f'{folder}/arquivo-captures.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False,
                    usecols=['captured_at_utc', 'target_url'])
    d['t'] = pd.to_datetime(d.captured_at_utc)
    return d

def peak(d):
    return int(d.t.dt.floor('min').value_counts().max())

rows = []  # (count, post says, post number, at least?, corpus number, note)
e = cap('01-education')
rows.append(('Education captures', 'more than 200,000', 200000, True, len(e), ''))
rows.append(('Education captures tagged "oai"', 'over 10,000', 10000, True, int(e.target_url.str.contains('zz=oai').sum()), ''))
c = cap('02-canada')
rows.append(('Canada captures', '899', 899, False, len(c), ''))
cs = pd.read_csv('02-canada/sources.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
rows.append(('Canada probe requests listed', '13', 13, False, int(cs.source_url.str.contains('/eng/Home/Record|ajax/count').sum()), ''))
k = cap('03-kansas')
rows.append(('Kansas captures', '36,578', 36578, False, len(k), ''))
rows.append(('Kansas peak per minute', '1,093', 1093, False, peak(k), ''))
rows.append(('Illinois captures', '251', 251, False, len(cap('04-illinois')), ''))
m = cap('05-maryland')
m6 = m[m.t.dt.date.astype(str) == '2026-05-06']
rows.append(('Maryland captures on May 6', '295,912', 295912, False, len(m6), ''))
rows.append(('Maryland peak per minute', '5,594', 5594, False, peak(m6), ''))
r = pd.read_csv('09-max-gov/urlquery-reports.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
h = pd.read_csv('09-max-gov/urlquery-http.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
rows.append(('MAX urlquery reports', '719', 719, False, len(r), ''))
named = r[~r.submitted_url.str.startswith('[WITHHELD')]
rows.append(('MAX distinct submitted URLs', '145', 145, False, named.submitted_url.nunique(),
             f' ({r.submitted_url.nunique()} with withheld ones)'))
rows.append(('MAX HTTP entries', '2,922', 2922, False, len(h), ''))
b = cap('12-bea')
rows.append(('BEA captures on apps.bea.gov', '3,005', 3005, False, int(b.target_url.str.contains('://apps.bea.gov').sum()), ''))

out = []
for name, said, n, at_least, got, note in rows:
    ok = got > n if at_least else got == n
    out.append((name, said, f'{got:,}{note}', 'match' if ok else f'{got - n:+,}'))
t = pd.DataFrame(out, columns=['count', 'post says', 'corpus has', 'difference']).set_index('count')
small = t.difference.ne('match') & t.difference.str.replace(',', '').str.lstrip('+-').str.isdigit()
print(f"{(t.difference == 'match').sum()} of {len(t)} match; "
      f"{(small & t.difference.str.replace(',', '').str.lstrip('+-').astype(float, errors='ignore').map(lambda x: abs(float(x)) <= 12 if str(x).replace('.', '').isdigit() else False)).sum()} differ by 12 or less")
t
